what: A Spend Cap / Cost Meter counts what every model call costs and keeps a running total per run, user, team and tenant. Before the next call it checks the cap, so a run stops calmly at its budget instead of surprising someone on the invoice.
like: Like a prepaid phone plan: every call ticks down the balance, and when it reaches zero the next call simply doesn't go through.
why: Agents loop; one stuck run can make thousands of calls
Tenants and teams need budgets they can trust
Cost per step shows which agent or prompt to fix first

steps.d: The run asks for one more model call. The cap check adds what it has spent to a worst-case estimate (max output tokens x price).
Under the cap, the call goes through the gateway, which counts real input and output tokens.
Tokens x price go into a ledger for the run, user, team and tenant, and into fast counters for the next check.
Over a hard cap the run stops or pauses with a clear status the user can see and top up.
A soft cap (say 80%) sends an alert instead of stopping.

numbers.l: budget_duration formats for LiteLLM budgets (no duration = never resets)
budget levels in LiteLLM: proxy, team, team member, user and virtual key (plus customers)

choices.d: Hard caps stop the run; soft caps alert. Use both: soft at ~80%, hard at 100%.
At the gateway every call passes through, not inside each agent, so no path can skip it.
If the meter's store is down, decide up front. LiteLLM notes budgets fail open without a database; for strict tenants fail closed.

instead.why: The gateway that does the counting

breaks.d: The cap is compared at the end of the run, after the money is spent.
breaks.fix: Check before every call with a worst-case estimate

breaks.d: Two calls pass the check at the same moment.
A new model price isn't in the table.
breaks.fix: Price table per model with a default, reconcile with the provider's usage

say: Every model call goes through one gateway that meters tokens x price per run, user, team and tenant.
I check the cap before each call with a worst-case estimate, so runs stop at the budget, not after it.
Soft cap alerts, hard cap stops with a clear status, and we reconcile with the provider's usage daily.

followups.q: How do you stop a runaway agent loop?
followups.a: A per-run budget and a max number of model and tool calls, both checked before each call.
The ledger is the source for usage-based billing, reconciled with provider invoices.

today: AI gateways (LiteLLM and cloud gateways) ship budgets per key, user, team and customer with reset periods.

check.q: When should the cap be checked?
check.why: After the call the money is already spent.

check.q: Two workers pass the check at once. What fixes it?
check.why: The check and the update must happen together.
